clue.text: Sea creature — lightweight animal lacking tail?

parts.note: a gram is a very light unit of weight

indicators.note: lacking its tail means the last letter of the cat word is dropped

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A riddle about a sea creature that is a lightweight animal with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A grampus is a sea mammal, Risso's dolphin or loosely the killer whale.

clue.text: Check cloth on seagoing vessel

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
re means on or concerning
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone inspects fabric aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an urge or feeling is to hold it back, the verb's synonym.

clue.text: Part of PM's article about Eton for broadcast

indicators.note: about means the article's two letters sit around the rest

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of Eton and for are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolboy piece about Eton put out on the radio for the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is the anagram signal and 'for' is part of the fodder. PM here is post meridiem, not the Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, covers the time after noon, so the afternoon is part of it.

clue.text: Upset workers' representatives in knockout event?

indicators.note: in places the union letters inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup competition is played on a knockout basis
TU is a trade union, which represents workers

explanation.surface: Union officials get upset at a knockout tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut up is an informal idiom for being distressed or upset.

clue.text: United supporters retreating in utter confusion

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the supporters' word is read in reverse

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
fans are a team's supporters

explanation.surface: Manchester United's fans go home in total disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' reads UFANS backwards as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu is military slang for a chaotic, botched situation, total muddle.

clue.text: Poignant end of sublime movement Arne loved at first

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of sublime is taken

parts.note: motion is movement

indicators.note: at first means the opening letters of Arne and loved are used

explanation.surface: A sublime musical movement by the composer Arne was loved at its first hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer; here his name supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poignant stirs the feelings, which is what an emotional scene does.

clue.text: Hooch nice boss distributed: there's no alternative

indicators.note: distributed means shared out, so the letters of the three words are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: A nice boss hands out moonshine, and nobody gets any other choice.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Thomas Hobson, a Cambridge stable keeper who made customers take the horse nearest the door or none.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a choice that is no real choice, take it or leave it.

clue.text: Terrified grass almost dispatched to arrest con

parts.note: panic is a kind of grass, panic grass

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold, so the shortened word wraps around the swindle
almost means the last letter of the dispatched word is dropped

parts.note: dispatched means sent
a trick is a con or swindle

explanation.surface: A police informer, nearly sent off, ends up nicking a con man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' tempts as British slang for an informer, but it is the plant, panic grass. 'almost' trims the dispatched word to SEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic-stricken describes someone overcome with fear, a near synonym.

clue.text: Send down girl who's out of practice, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a Kate who is rusty, out of practice, gives the spoken phrase Rusty Kate

explanation.surface: A girl is sent down because she has let her skills lapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Send down is British university slang for expelling a student, and to rusticate is to suspend one temporarily, sending them to the country.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge, rusticating a student means suspending them, sending them down from university.

clue.text: Heavenly body hugging right pillock!

indicators.note: hugging means the satellite wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: the moon is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a celestial body embracing a right idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Pillock is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insults for a stupid person, pillock being British slang.

clue.text: Eat voraciously, being a large bird

definitions.meaning: an old verb sense: to devour food greedily
a large black member of the crow family

explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the big black crow; the verb, now rare, means to devour ravenously.

clue.text: Rapacious secretary squeezing leftist politician

indicators.note: squeezing means the assistant's letters press around the left-winger

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
a red is a left-winger
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A grasping secretary hugs a left-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Predatory behaviour is greedy and exploitative, like a rapacious person's.

clue.text: Pub row? It's divisive, with staff backing

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out in a pub, splitting the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is the musical stave: a bar line is drawn on it to divide one bar from the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical bar line divides music into bars, drawn across the stave behind it.

clue.text: Conscript taking stupid directions without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the stupid word goes round the symbol

parts.note: daft means stupid
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
E and E are two compass directions, east twice

explanation.surface: A conscript follows silly orders without putting up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is someone drafted, or conscripted, into military service.

clue.text: Abstracted, as a schooner may be?

definitions.meaning: absent-minded, with a blank, vacant stare
a schooner is also a large drinking glass, so it is made of glass

explanation.definitionFit: A glassy look is expressionless and vacant; a schooner glass is literally made of glass.

clue.text: Wiles a rising Asian ruler employed to get fleece

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading the word upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: arts are wiles or cunning tricks
a khan is a ruler in central Asia

explanation.surface: An Asian ruler uses cunning tricks to obtain a sheepskin.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is the curly fleece of young karakul lambs, named after the Russian city.

clue.text: Disconcert agent over clumsy boat crossing river

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, so read in reverse

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent

indicators.note: crossing means the boat word spans the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: A salesman unsettles the passengers aboard an awkward boat crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb someone is to unsettle or disconcert them, a synonym.

clue.text: Most of masonry at entrance to this plant

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the masonry word is dropped

parts.note: stonework is masonry

indicators.note: entrance to means the opening letter of this is taken

explanation.surface: Nearly all the masonry at a doorway is overgrown by this plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewort is a green alga, a freshwater plant encrusted with lime.

clue.text: Work taking place in Republican party?

indicators.note: in places the happening word inside the Republican and party letters

parts.note: a do is a party
on means happening or taking place

explanation.surface: A job is under way at a Republican party gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical work whose main theme keeps returning.

clue.text: Wanting sustenance, a bit like Gregory?

definitions.meaning: somewhat resembling the actor Gregory Peck, with -ish meaning rather like

explanation.definitionFit: Peckish is British for feeling a little hungry; read as Peck-ish it means a bit like Gregory Peck.

clue.text: Consumed game, a tender part

indicators.note: part means only a section of the words game, a tender is used

explanation.surface: A tender cut of game was eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten and consumed are synonyms for having been devoured.

clue.text: More flexible cover for current purveyor of goods

indicators.note: cover for means the flexible word wraps around the current symbol

parts.note: suppler means more flexible
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A more adaptable insurance policy for an electricity provider.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplier is one who provides or sells goods, a purveyor.

clue.text: Animal minder's novel way to secure tent, for example

indicators.note: to secure means to hold, so the novel and road letters close round the drink

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, so an example of wine
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A minder's new method for pegging down a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tent' is not camping gear but a red wine from Spain; 'novel' is not an adjective but Haggard's She.
explanation.definitionFit: A swineherd tends pigs, so is a minder of animals.

clue.text: Miners not working at deepest level?

indicators.note: working signals that the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Miners not at work are down at the deepest seam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' looks like one phrase, but 'not' is fodder and 'working' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Innermost means furthest in, the deepest point, as miners would be.

clue.text: Close relative fed by person cutting piece of pork

indicators.note: fed by means the relative takes the cutter inside it

parts.note: a sib is a sibling, a close relative
a parer is someone who pares or trims

explanation.surface: A sibling is given food by someone carving pork.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparerib is a cut of pork from the ribs.

clue.text: Character opposed to alcoholic drink

parts.note: chi is a Greek letter, a character
anti means against or opposed to

explanation.surface: A person of temperance takes a stand against drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Capital a male ally invested in Kazakhstan's leaders

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so these letters go within the two leading letters

parts.note: the first two letters of Kazakhstan, its leading letters
a pal is a friend or ally

explanation.surface: Money from a male ally is put into Kazakhstan by its leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Kampala is the capital city of Uganda.

clue.text: Biochemical catalyst unknown in parts of Yemen

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the rearranged letters
parts of Yemen means its letters broken up and rearranged

parts.note: z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: An unidentified catalyst is found in regions of Yemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' turns YEMEN into ENYME, and 'in' puts Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a protein that speeds up biochemical reactions, a catalyst.

clue.text: One who delivers, except on third of March?

parts.note: save means except, as in all save one

indicators.note: third of means the third letter of March is taken

explanation.surface: A delivery person working every day apart from a date in March.
explanation.definitionFit: A saver rescues or delivers people, as a saviour does.

clue.text: Generous former partner withdrawing from case

indicators.note: withdrawing from means the partner leaves the case word

parts.note: an example is a case or instance
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A generous ex pulls out of a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful or generous in amount.
